subproblem.title: Uniform lower Lipschitz bound for an injective C¹ immersion on a compact set (step 2, lower bound)
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^d be open and K ⊆ U compact, and let g : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be C¹ on U (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U). Assume g is injective on K and Dg(z) = fderiv ℝ g z is injective for every z ∈ K. Then there is m > 0 such that m|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| for all a, b ∈ K (Euclidean norms).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (g : Euclid d → Euclid P) (U K : Set (Euclid d)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U → InjOn g K → (∀ z ∈ K, Injective (fderiv ℝ g z)) → ∃ m : ℝ, 0 < m ∧ ∀ a ∈ K, ∀ b ∈ K, m * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖g a - g b‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 2 ("Lower") of the parent proof: "there is m > 0 with |g(a) − g(b)| ≥ m|a − b| for a, b ∈ B̄. Otherwise there are a_k ≠ b_k in B̄ with |g(a_k) − g(b_k)| < k⁻¹|a_k − b_k|. By compactness, pass to a subsequence with a_k → a, b_k → b, and e_k := (a_k − b_k)/|a_k − b_k| → e with |e| = 1. If a ≠ b, continuity gives g(a) = g(b), contradicting injectivity on B̄. If a = b, … |Dg(a)e| = lim_k |g(a_k) − g(b_k)|/|a_k − b_k| = 0, contradicting injectivity of Dg(a)." The parent applies this child with K = B̄ = closedBall(c, r), which is compact in ℝ^d. The only change is that B̄ is replaced by an arbitrary compact K ⊆ U. Accordingly the segment estimate of the case a = b is taken on a small ball around a inside U, where it is the mean value inequality; convexity of K is not needed.

Notation. |·| is the Euclidean norm; S := {e ∈ ℝ^d : |e| = 1}.

1. (Local facts at points of K.) Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U and U is open, so U is a neighbourhood of x on which g is C¹; hence g is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). In particular:
 (a) g is continuous at x;
 (b) g is strictly differentiable at x with derivative L_x := Dg(x): for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that |g(y) − g(y') − L_x(y − y')| ≤ ε|y − y'| for all y, y' ∈ ball(x, δ).
 Proof of (b). Dg is continuous on the open set U because g is C¹ there. Choose δ > 0 with ball(x, δ) ⊆ U and ‖Dg(w) − L_x‖ ≤ ε for all w ∈ ball(x, δ). The map ψ(w) := g(w) − L_x w is differentiable on the convex set ball(x, δ) with ‖Dψ(w)‖ = ‖Dg(w) − L_x‖ ≤ ε. The mean value inequality gives |ψ(y) − ψ(y')| ≤ ε|y − y'| for y, y' ∈ ball(x, δ), which is the claim. (Mathlib packages (b) as ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt: HasStrictFDerivAt g (fderiv ℝ g x) x, whose isLittleO form says g(y) − g(y') − L_x(y − y') = o(|y − y'|) as (y, y') → (x, x).)

2. (Contradiction hypothesis.) Suppose no m > 0 has the stated property. Then for each k ∈ ℕ, applying this to m = 1/(k + 1) > 0, there are a_k, b_k ∈ K with
 |g(a_k) − g(b_k)| < (k + 1)⁻¹ |a_k − b_k|.   (∗)

3. (a_k ≠ b_k.) If |a_k − b_k| = 0, the right side of (∗) is 0 and (∗) would make a norm negative, which is impossible. So |a_k − b_k| > 0, and e_k := |a_k − b_k|⁻¹ (a_k − b_k) satisfies |e_k| = |a_k − b_k|⁻¹ |a_k − b_k| = 1, i.e. e_k ∈ S.

4. (Convergent subsequence.) K is compact, and S is compact (closed and bounded in the finite-dimensional space ℝ^d). So K × K × S is compact, and it contains (a_k, b_k, e_k) for every k. By sequential compactness there are (a, b, e) ∈ K × K × S and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with a_{φ(k)} → a, b_{φ(k)} → b and e_{φ(k)} → e. In particular a, b ∈ K and |e| = 1. Since φ(k) ≥ k, (φ(k) + 1)⁻¹ → 0.

5. (Case a ≠ b.) By 1(a) at a and at b, g(a_{φ(k)}) → g(a) and g(b_{φ(k)}) → g(b), so g(a_{φ(k)}) − g(b_{φ(k)}) → g(a) − g(b). By (∗),
 0 ≤ |g(a_{φ(k)}) − g(b_{φ(k)})| ≤ (φ(k) + 1)⁻¹ |a_{φ(k)} − b_{φ(k)}|,
 and the right side tends to 0 · |a − b| = 0. By the squeeze principle g(a_{φ(k)}) − g(b_{φ(k)}) → 0, so by uniqueness of limits g(a) − g(b) = 0. Thus g(a) = g(b) with a, b ∈ K and a ≠ b, contradicting the injectivity of g on K.

6. (Case a = b.) Put L := Dg(a); this is defined with a ∈ K. Write d_k := |a_{φ(k)} − b_{φ(k)}| > 0. Since e_{φ(k)} = d_k⁻¹(a_{φ(k)} − b_{φ(k)}) and L is linear,
 L e_{φ(k)} = d_k⁻¹ (g(a_{φ(k)}) − g(b_{φ(k)})) − d_k⁻¹ (g(a_{φ(k)}) − g(b_{φ(k)}) − L(a_{φ(k)} − b_{φ(k)})).
 Taking norms, and using (∗) on the first term,
 |L e_{φ(k)}| ≤ (φ(k) + 1)⁻¹ + |g(a_{φ(k)}) − g(b_{φ(k)}) − L(a_{φ(k)} − b_{φ(k)})| / d_k.
 The first term tends to 0 by step 4. For the second term, let ε > 0 and take δ from 1(b) at x = a. Since a_{φ(k)} → a and b_{φ(k)} → a, both points lie in ball(a, δ) for all large k, and then the quotient is ≤ ε. So the second term also tends to 0. By the squeeze principle, |L e_{φ(k)}| → 0. On the other hand L is a continuous linear map, so L e_{φ(k)} → L e and |L e_{φ(k)}| → |L e|. By uniqueness of limits |L e| = 0. Then L e = 0 = L 0, and injectivity of L = Dg(a) gives e = 0, contradicting |e| = 1.

7. (Conclusion.) Both cases are impossible, so the hypothesis of step 2 is false. Hence there is m > 0 with m|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| for all a, b ∈ K. ∎

```lean
theorem Submission.dtc_bc_lc_sl_c1t_lower_lipschitz : (∀ (P d : ℕ) (g : Euclid d → Euclid P) (U K : Set (Euclid d)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U → InjOn g K → (∀ z ∈ K, Injective (fderiv ℝ g z)) → ∃ m : ℝ, 0 < m ∧ ∀ a ∈ K, ∀ b ∈ K, m * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖g a - g b‖) := by
  intro P d g U K hU hK hKU hg hinj hDinj
  by_contra hcon
  push Not at hcon
  -- Steps 2–3: for each `k` there are `a_k ≠ b_k` in `K` with `|g a_k - g b_k| < (k + 1)⁻¹ |a_k - b_k|`
  choose a ha b hb hab using fun k : ℕ => hcon (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) (by positivity)
  have hpos : ∀ k, 0 < ‖a k - b k‖ := by
    intro k
    have h1 := hab k
    have h2 := norm_nonneg (g (a k) - g (b k))
    by_contra hle
    push Not at hle
    have h0 : ‖a k - b k‖ = 0 := le_antisymm hle (norm_nonneg _)
    rw [h0, mul_zero] at h1
    linarith
  -- Steps 3–4: unit vectors `e_k` and a convergent subsequence
  set e : ℕ → Euclid d := fun k => ‖a k - b k‖⁻¹ • (a k - b k) with he_def
  have he : ∀ k, e k ∈ sphere (0 : Euclid d) 1 := by
    intro k
    rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, he_def]
    simp only [norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm]
    exact inv_mul_cancel₀ (hpos k).ne'
  obtain ⟨⟨a0, b0, e0⟩, ⟨ha0, hb0, he0⟩, φ, hφ, hlim⟩ :=
    (hK.prod (hK.prod (isCompact_sphere (0 : Euclid d) 1))).tendsto_subseq
      (x := fun k => (a k, b k, e k)) (fun k => ⟨ha k, hb k, he k⟩)
  have hla : Tendsto (fun k => a (φ k)) atTop (𝓝 a0) := (continuous_fst.tendsto _).comp hlim
  have hlb : Tendsto (fun k => b (φ k)) atTop (𝓝 b0) :=
    ((continuous_fst.comp continuous_snd).tendsto _).comp hlim
  have hle : Tendsto (fun k => e (φ k)) atTop (𝓝 e0) :=
    ((continuous_snd.comp continuous_snd).tendsto _).comp hlim
  have hinvk : Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => 1 / ((φ k : ℝ) + 1)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat).comp hφ.tendsto_atTop
  by_cases hab0 : a0 = b0
  · -- Step 6: `a = b`; strict differentiability of `g` at `a` forces `Dg(a) e = 0`
    subst hab0
    have hstrict : HasStrictFDerivAt g (fderiv ℝ g a0) a0 :=
      (hg.contDiffAt (hU.mem_nhds (hKU ha0))).hasStrictFDerivAt one_ne_zero
    have hpair : Tendsto (fun k => (a (φ k), b (φ k))) atTop (𝓝 (a0, a0)) := hla.prodMk_nhds hlb
    have ho := (hstrict.isLittleO.comp_tendsto hpair).norm_norm.tendsto_div_nhds_zero
    -- `|Dg(a)e_k| ≤ |g a_k - g b_k| / |a_k - b_k| + o(1) → 0`
    have hbound : ∀ k, ‖fderiv ℝ g a0 (e (φ k))‖ ≤ 1 / ((φ k : ℝ) + 1) +
        ‖g (a (φ k)) - g (b (φ k)) - fderiv ℝ g a0 (a (φ k) - b (φ k))‖ / ‖a (φ k) - b (φ k)‖ := by
      intro k
      have hk := hpos (φ k)
      have hdec : fderiv ℝ g a0 (e (φ k)) = ‖a (φ k) - b (φ k)‖⁻¹ • (g (a (φ k)) - g (b (φ k))) -
          ‖a (φ k) - b (φ k)‖⁻¹ • (g (a (φ k)) - g (b (φ k)) - fderiv ℝ g a0 (a (φ k) - b (φ k))) := by
        rw [he_def, map_smul, ← smul_sub, sub_sub_cancel]
      rw [hdec]
      refine (norm_sub_le _ _).trans (add_le_add ?_ ?_)
      · rw [norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm, inv_mul_le_iff₀ hk]
        have := (hab (φ k)).le
        linarith [mul_comm (1 / ((φ k : ℝ) + 1)) ‖a (φ k) - b (φ k)‖]
      · rw [norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm, div_eq_inv_mul]
    have htend : Tendsto (fun k => ‖fderiv ℝ g a0 (e (φ k))‖) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      refine squeeze_zero (fun k => norm_nonneg _) hbound ?_
      simpa using hinvk.add ho
    have hL : Tendsto (fun k => ‖fderiv ℝ g a0 (e (φ k))‖) atTop (𝓝 ‖fderiv ℝ g a0 e0‖) :=
      (((fderiv ℝ g a0).continuous.tendsto _).comp hle).norm
    have hL0 : fderiv ℝ g a0 e0 = 0 := norm_eq_zero.1 (tendsto_nhds_unique hL htend)
    have he00 : e0 = 0 := hDinj a0 ha0 (by rw [hL0, map_zero])
    rw [he00, mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_zero] at he0
    exact zero_ne_one he0
  · -- Step 5: `a ≠ b`; continuity of `g` forces `g a = g b`
    have hcont : ∀ x ∈ K, ContinuousAt g x := fun x hx =>
      (hg.contDiffAt (hU.mem_nhds (hKU hx))).continuousAt
    have hga : Tendsto (fun k => g (a (φ k))) atTop (𝓝 (g a0)) := (hcont a0 ha0).tendsto.comp hla
    have hgb : Tendsto (fun k => g (b (φ k))) atTop (𝓝 (g b0)) := (hcont b0 hb0).tendsto.comp hlb
    have hdiff : Tendsto (fun k => g (a (φ k)) - g (b (φ k))) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      rw [tendsto_zero_iff_norm_tendsto_zero]
      have hbd : Tendsto (fun k => 1 / ((φ k : ℝ) + 1) * ‖a (φ k) - b (φ k)‖) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
        simpa using hinvk.mul (hla.sub hlb).norm
      exact squeeze_zero (fun k => norm_nonneg _) (fun k => (hab (φ k)).le) hbd
    have hzero : g a0 - g b0 = 0 := tendsto_nhds_unique (hga.sub hgb) hdiff
    exact hab0 (hinj ha0 hb0 (sub_eq_zero.1 hzero))
```
proof_key_steps: Suppose not: for each k pick a_k, b_k ∈ K with |g(a_k) − g(b_k)| < (k+1)⁻¹|a_k − b_k|; then a_k ≠ b_k and e_k = (a_k − b_k)/|a_k − b_k| is a unit vector.
By compactness of K × K × S^{d−1}, a subsequence has a_{φ(k)} → a ∈ K, b_{φ(k)} → b ∈ K and e_{φ(k)} → e with |e| = 1.
If a ≠ b, continuity of g at a and b gives g(a) = g(b), contradicting injectivity of g on K.
If a = b, strict differentiability of the C¹ map g at a (mean value inequality near a) gives |Dg(a)e_{φ(k)}| ≤ (φ(k)+1)⁻¹ + o(1) → 0, so Dg(a)e = 0 with |e| = 1, contradicting injectivity of Dg(a).

subproblem.title: Dominated convergence of the rescaled area integrals on a compact neighbourhood (steps 4–6)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, h : ℝ^n → ℝ, B ⊆ ℝ^n, z ∈ ℝ^n, m ∈ ℝ and f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Assume: B is compact and is a neighbourhood of z; g and h are continuous on B; g is differentiable at z; m > 0; m|a − z| ≤ |g(a) − g(z)| for every a ∈ B; m|v| ≤ |Dg(z)v| for every v ∈ ℝ^n, where Dg(z) = fderiv ℝ g z; f is continuous with compact support. Then, as s ↓ 0 (along 𝓝[>] 0), ∫_{B_s} h(z + sb)·f(s⁻¹(g(z + sb) − g(z))) db → h(z)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Dg(z)b) db, where B_s := {b ∈ ℝ^n : z + sb ∈ B}. Both are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (z : Euclid n) (m : ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), IsCompact B → B ∈ 𝓝 z → ContinuousOn g B → DifferentiableAt ℝ g z → ContinuousOn h B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, m * ‖a - z‖ ≤ ‖g a - g z‖) → (∀ v : Euclid n, m * ‖v‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ g z v‖) → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ∫ b in {b : Euclid n | z + s • b ∈ B}, h (z + s • b) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (h z * ∫ b, f (fderiv ℝ g z b)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 4–6 of the parent proof: domination via the lower Lipschitz bound, the pointwise limit, and dominated convergence along the countably generated filter s ↓ 0. It also includes the identification of the limit integral that precedes step 7. The parent applies this child with:
- B = B̄ = closedBall(c, r), which is compact and is a neighbourhood of z because z ∈ ball(c, r);
- the given g;
- the weight h(a) := J(Dg(a)) = √det(Dg(a)* ∘ Dg(a)), continuous on B̄ because Dg is continuous on the open U ⊇ B̄;
- the constant m of step 2 (the child lower_lipschitz) and the bound m|v| ≤ |Dg(z)v| (the child fderiv_lower_bound);
- f the test function.
The Jacobian is abstracted into a weight h that is continuous on B. Then the upper bound J ≤ J_max of step 2 follows from compactness of B (step 6 below). This child is the compact-neighbourhood analogue of the comparator-accepted DAG lemma codim1_rdo_c1pt_rescaled_integral_tendsto, which assumes g and h continuous on all of ℝ^n and B open. Neither holds in the parent: g is C¹ only on U, and the parent integrates over the closed ball. So the argument is given in full.

Notation. L := Dg(z) = fderiv ℝ g z. For s > 0: G_s(b) := s⁻¹(g(z + sb) − g(z)), F_s(b) := h(z + sb)·f(G_s(b)), B_s := {b ∈ ℝ^n : z + sb ∈ B}. All integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n.

1. (Support radius.) tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R > 0. Thus f(y) = 0 whenever |y| > R.

2. (Inner ball.) B is a neighbourhood of z, so ball(z, ε) ⊆ B for some ε > 0. With ρ := ε/2 > 0, closedBall(z, ρ) ⊆ ball(z, ε) ⊆ B.

3. (Small scales.) Put s₀ := mρ/R > 0 and K := closedBall(0, R/m). Let 0 < s ≤ s₀ and b ∈ K. Then |(z + sb) − z| = s|b| ≤ (mρ/R)(R/m) = ρ, so z + sb ∈ closedBall(z, ρ) ⊆ B. Hence K ⊆ B_s.

4. (Vanishing off K.) Let s > 0, b ∈ B_s and b ∉ K, so |b| > R/m, i.e. R < m|b|. The hypothesis with a = z + sb ∈ B gives m·s|b| = m|(z + sb) − z| ≤ |g(z + sb) − g(z)|. Hence |G_s(b)| = s⁻¹|g(z + sb) − g(z)| ≥ m|b| > R. So f(G_s(b)) = 0 by step 1, and F_s(b) = 0.

5. (Localisation to K.) B is compact, hence closed. B_s is the preimage of B under the continuous map b ↦ z + sb, so B_s is closed and measurable. Let 0 < s < s₀. Then K ⊆ B_s by step 3, and F_s = 0 on B_s \ K by step 4. Hence ∫_{B_s} F_s = ∫_K F_s. (For a measurable set and a subset of it, the two set integrals agree when the integrand vanishes on the difference; no integrability is needed. Mathlib: setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero.)

6. (Uniform bound.) h is continuous on the compact set B, so |h| ≤ Λ on B for some Λ. f is continuous with compact support, so |f| ≤ C on ℝ^P for some C. Let 0 < s < s₀ and b ∈ K. Then z + sb ∈ B by step 3, so |F_s(b)| ≤ ΛC. The constant ΛC is integrable on K, which has finite Lebesgue measure.

7. (Measurability.) Let 0 < s < s₀. The continuous map b ↦ z + sb sends K into B (step 3). Since h and g are continuous on B and f is continuous, F_s is continuous on K. As K is closed, F_s is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to K.

8. (Pointwise limit.) Fix b ∈ ℝ^n.
- As s → 0, z + sb → z. Moreover h is continuous at z, since it is continuous on B and B is a neighbourhood of z. So h(z + sb) → h(z).
- g is differentiable at z with derivative L, so g(z + w) − g(z) − Lw = o(|w|) as w → 0. With w = sb this gives G_s(b) − Lb = s⁻¹(g(z + sb) − g(z) − L(sb)) → 0 as s ↓ 0, i.e. G_s(b) → Lb. (Mathlib: HasFDerivAt.lim with c(s) = s⁻¹, where |c(s)| → ∞ along 𝓝[>] 0.)
- f is continuous, so f(G_s(b)) → f(Lb).
Hence F_s(b) → h(z)·f(Lb) as s ↓ 0, for every b.

9. (Dominated convergence.) The filter 𝓝[>] 0 is countably generated. On K, steps 6–8 give eventual a.e.-strong measurability, an eventual uniform integrable bound, and pointwise convergence. The dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) therefore gives ∫_K F_s → ∫_K h(z)·f(Lb) db as s ↓ 0.

10. (Identification of the limit.) Let b ∉ K. Then |b| > R/m, and the hypothesis on L gives |Lb| ≥ m|b| > R, so f(Lb) = 0. Hence ∫_K h(z) f(Lb) db = ∫_{ℝ^n} h(z) f(Lb) db = h(z)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lb) db (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, integral_const_mul).

11. (Conclusion.) By step 5, ∫_{B_s} F_s = ∫_K F_s for all s ∈ (0, s₀), hence eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. By steps 9 and 10, ∫_K F_s → h(z)·∫ f(Lb) db. Therefore ∫_{B_s} h(z + sb) f(s⁻¹(g(z + sb) − g(z))) db → h(z)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Dg(z)b) db as s ↓ 0. ∎

theorem Submission.dtc_bc_lc_sl_c1t_rescaled_tendsto : (∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (z : Euclid n) (m : ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), IsCompact B → B ∈ 𝓝 z → ContinuousOn g B → DifferentiableAt ℝ g z → ContinuousOn h B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, m * ‖a - z‖ ≤ ‖g a - g z‖) → (∀ v : Euclid n, m * ‖v‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ g z v‖) → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ∫ b in {b : Euclid n | z + s • b ∈ B}, h (z + s • b) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (h z * ∫ b, f (fderiv ℝ g z b)))) := by
  intro P n g h B z m f hBc hBz hg hgz hh hm hgB hL hf hfs
  -- Step 1: `f = 0` off `closedBall 0 R`
  obtain ⟨R, hR, hRf⟩ : ∃ R : ℝ, 0 < R ∧ ∀ y, R < ‖y‖ → f y = 0 := by
    obtain ⟨R, hR, hsub⟩ := hfs.isCompact.isBounded.subset_closedBall_lt 0 0
    refine ⟨R, hR, fun y hy => ?_⟩
    by_contra hne
    have hy' := hsub (subset_tsupport f hne)
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] at hy'
    linarith
  -- Step 2: `closedBall z ρ ⊆ B`
  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ, hρB⟩ : ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ closedBall z ρ ⊆ B := by
    obtain ⟨ε, hε, hεB⟩ := Metric.mem_nhds_iff.1 hBz
    exact ⟨ε / 2, half_pos hε, (closedBall_subset_ball (half_lt_self hε)).trans hεB⟩
  -- Steps 3–4: `K = closedBall 0 (R / m)`, `s₀ = m ρ / R`; the integrand vanishes on `B_s \ K`
  have hs₀ : 0 < m * ρ / R := div_pos (mul_pos hm hρ) hR
  have hKB : ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ m * ρ / R → ∀ b ∈ closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m),
      z + s • b ∈ B := by
    intro s hs hss b hb
    apply hρB
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] at hb
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm, add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg hs.le]
    calc s * ‖b‖ ≤ m * ρ / R * (R / m) := mul_le_mul hss hb (norm_nonneg _) hs₀.le
      _ = ρ := by field_simp
  have hout : ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∀ b : Euclid n, z + s • b ∈ B →
      b ∉ closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m) → f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z)) = 0 := by
    intro s hs b hbB hbK
    apply hRf
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, not_le, div_lt_iff₀ hm] at hbK
    have h1 := hgB _ hbB
    rw [add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg hs.le] at h1
    rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.2 hs.le)]
    calc R < ‖b‖ * m := hbK
      _ = s⁻¹ * (m * (s * ‖b‖)) := by field_simp
      _ ≤ s⁻¹ * ‖g (z + s • b) - g z‖ := by gcongr
  -- Step 5: localisation to `K`
  have hloc : ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),
      (∫ b in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), h (z + s • b) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z))) =
        ∫ b in {b : Euclid n | z + s • b ∈ B}, h (z + s • b) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z)) := by
    filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsGT hs₀] with s hs
    symm
    apply setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero
    · exact (hBc.isClosed.preimage (continuous_const.add (continuous_const_smul s))).measurableSet
    · intro b hb
      exact hKB s hs.1 hs.2.le b hb
    · rintro b ⟨hbB, hbK⟩
      rw [hout s hs.1 b hbB hbK, mul_zero]
  -- Step 6: uniform bounds
  obtain ⟨Λ, hΛ⟩ := hBc.exists_bound_of_continuousOn hh
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hf.bounded_above_of_compact_support hfs
  -- Steps 7–9: measurability, pointwise limit and dominated convergence on `K`
  have hdom : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ∫ b in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m),
      h (z + s • b) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z))) (𝓝[>] 0)
      (𝓝 (∫ b in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), h z * f (fderiv ℝ g z b))) := by
    refine tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence (fun _ => Λ * C) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsGT hs₀] with s hs
      have hz : Continuous fun b : Euclid n => z + s • b :=
        continuous_const.add (continuous_const_smul s)
      have hmaps : MapsTo (fun b : Euclid n => z + s • b) (closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m)) B :=
        fun b hb => hKB s hs.1 hs.2.le b hb
      have hcont : ContinuousOn (fun b : Euclid n => h (z + s • b) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z)))
          (closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m)) :=
        (hh.comp hz.continuousOn hmaps).mul (hf.comp_continuousOn
          (((hg.comp hz.continuousOn hmaps).sub continuousOn_const).const_smul s⁻¹))
      exact hcont.aestronglyMeasurable measurableSet_closedBall
    · filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsGT hs₀] with s hs
      filter_upwards [ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_closedBall] with b hb
      have hmem := hKB s hs.1 hs.2.le b hb
      rw [norm_mul]
      exact mul_le_mul (hΛ _ hmem) (hC _) (norm_nonneg _) ((norm_nonneg _).trans (hΛ _ hmem))
    · exact integrableOn_const measure_closedBall_lt_top.ne
    · refine Eventually.of_forall fun b => Tendsto.mul ?_ ?_
      · -- `h (z + s • b) → h z`
        have h1 : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => z + s • b) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (z + (0 : ℝ) • b)) :=
          (continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const)).tendsto 0
        rw [zero_smul, add_zero] at h1
        exact (hh.continuousAt hBz).tendsto.comp (h1.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds)
      · -- difference quotients: `s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z) → L b`
        have hc : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ‖s⁻¹‖) (𝓝[>] 0) atTop :=
          tendsto_norm_atTop_atTop.comp tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero
        have hlim := hgz.hasFDerivAt.lim b hc
        simp only [inv_inv] at hlim
        exact (hf.tendsto _).comp hlim
  -- Step 10: identification of the limit
  have hid : ∫ b in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), h z * f (fderiv ℝ g z b) =
      h z * ∫ b, f (fderiv ℝ g z b) := by
    rw [setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, integral_const_mul]
    intro b hb
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, not_le, div_lt_iff₀ hm] at hb
    rw [hRf _ (hb.trans_le ((mul_comm _ _).le.trans (hL b))), mul_zero]
  rw [← hid]
  exact hdom.congr' hloc

proof_key_steps: Choose R with f = 0 off closedBall(0, R) and ρ with closedBall(z, ρ) ⊆ B; for 0 < s < s₀ = mρ/R the ball K = closedBall(0, R/m) satisfies z + sK ⊆ B.
The lower bound m|a − z| ≤ |g(a) − g(z)| on B gives |G_s(b)| ≥ m|b| > R off K, so the integral over B_s equals the integral over K for 0 < s < s₀.
On K the integrand is continuous, bounded by sup_B|h|·sup|f| (B compact), and converges pointwise to h(z)f(Dg(z)b) (continuity of h at z, differentiability of g at z).
Dominated convergence along 𝓝[>]0 and f(Dg(z)b) = 0 off K (from m|v| ≤ |Dg(z)v|) give the limit h(z)∫ f(Dg(z)b) db.
